problem_text: This instance describes dispatch planning for short-haul container moves around a terminal and its nearby transfer points. There are 105 transport orders and 105 available chassis. The planner must decide a one-to-one pairing so that every order is covered and every chassis is used exactly once. Pairing is allowed for any order-chassis combination; the data provide explicit cost entries for some pairings and all other pairings use an implicit baseline cost of 0. The plan also tracks 65 event timestamps for key visits or handoffs. Operational policies are given as standardized rule records that link pairing choices to timing consistency requirements and to shared-facility limits aggregated over a single referenced order set (the set may cover only a subset of orders). In this instance, each order has a designated primary chassis option that shares the same identifier as the order, and timing-shift rules describe how the required time gap changes when switching from that primary option to an alternative. Each rule table uses a uniform comparison direction code, given by G for timing-shift rules and G for group-aggregation rules. Timing-shift rules also rely on a shared large adjustment constant 60000. All identifiers in the data files are zero-based. The goal is to find a feasible plan with minimum total cost.
